newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's ABAL sees record 1996 aluminium demand.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's ABAL sees record 1996 aluminium demand.

text.p: Brazilian consumption of downstream aluminium products is predicted to rise 10.9 percent in 1996 to a record 558,000 tonnes, according to the latest estimate from the Brazilian Aluminium Association (ABAL).
This is also an increase from a March forecast of 536,700 tonnes, it added.
Primary aluminium production however is only expected to rise slightly to just under 1.2 million tonnes against 1.19 million tonnes produced in 1995.
Exports are also seen climbing by 9.1 percent to 871,100 tonnes from 798,500 tonnes last year. However in March ABAL had hoped overseas sales would reach 944,500 tonnes.
Of this year's total, 771,800 tonnes of exports should be of primary aluminium and alloys, up 9.8 percent from 1995.
Moreover imports are forecast to fall 7.4 percent to 88,900 tonnes from 96,000 tonnes in 1995.
Internal sales of primary aluminium are expected to hold steady through the second half of the year after first starting to improve upon 1995 performance in July.
Sales in August reached 18,500 tonnes, up from 12,100 tonnes in the same month last year, and are forecast around 17,000 tonnes per month until the end of the year.
This would give total sales of 196,300 tonnes in 1996 against 190,700 tonnes last year, ABAL said.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
